properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/02/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Derry Township, Westmoreland county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/02/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8154407
Permit API: 129-27013
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Derry Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/02/2023
Comments: On August 2, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill report. The spill was called in to the Department today at 9:54 AM by the Operator, who described a 25-26 barrel release of crude oil that was found by a well tender at 8:40 AM. Operator will be utilizing Act 2 standards for clean up.The Department arrived on site at approximately 1:15 PM and spoke with Paul Steiner of Diversified. According to Steiner, a well tender discovered the release at approximately 8:40 AM from a crack (Photo 3) in the storage/production tank on site. Steiner approximated the total release to be 26 barrels based on the amount of crude oil in the production tank last week (approximately 4 feet) and the amount of crude oil still in the tank at discovery, which is an approximate 22 inches.The release migrated towards and past the production equipment (Photo 4) and down an embankment, where it reportedly stopped at a berm (Photo 8) according to Steiner. Steiner is using a PID meter to detect the extent of the oil's migration. During the on site inspection, Diversified was excavating impacted material at the berm and moving it upslope so that they can place it into a Spartan dump truck to have it transported for disposal. Steiner says one truck load will be transported tonight, excavation will stop, then another Spartan truck will arrive tomorrow morning, excavation will resume, and remaining impacted material will be taken off site before Moody arrives in the afternoon to confirm complete site clean up. Oil absorbent booms will be placed around and downslope of the impacted material overnight tonight to prevent further migration between truck loads, according to Steiner.Following the inspection, Steiner and myself spoke with DCNR Park Manager Kris Baker of Keystone State Park at the park office to notify the park of the release.Violations issued for spill. The Department requests disposal documents when made available.

Comments: On 04/04/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 Well Site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). On 03/11/2024, the violations were issued as outstanding (IR 3726997). The operator was in compliance with schedule on 03/27/2024 (IR 3736262).The following was observed during inspection on 04/04/2024:Inspection conducted after several large rain events. The beginning upper part of the channel was displaying accelerated erosion and rills entering the channel (Photos 1, 2). The opposite side of the road was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. Sediment accumulation was noted within the stabilized area with establishing vegetation (Photos 3, 4). Upper culvert inlet was blocked with sediment (Photo 5).Several sections of the bank above the channel did not have temporary stabilization. A section of open soils was displaying rills leading into the channel. The channel was also displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation (Photos 6, 7).The middle culvert was completely blocked with sediment. Gravel was noted above the inlet, flowing over towards the channel. Debris and channelization were noted leaving the culvert inlet (Photos 8-10).The outlet of the middle culvert had sediment accumulation within the grass and accelerated erosion below (Photos 11-15).Outlet of roadside channel was displaying accelerated erosion and sedimentation. It was noted that sediment and flow were also both coming from the direction of the Landowner's building, in addition to the site's channel. Sediment accumulation within vegetation leading to the collection box and the site's middle culvert (Photos 16-20).Sediment accumulation within culvert and the outlet. This leads towards the stream (Photos 21, 22).Several rills leading off site and towards the roadside channel near the beginning section of the access road (Photos 23, 24). Remnants of gravel/sediment noted leading off the beginning of the access road towards the main township road (Photo 25).The violations issued on 03/11/2024 remain outstanding. A violation of 102.22(b)1 is being issued for the lack of temporary stabilization and the associated accelerated erosion.

Comments: Well inspection conducted as an ongoing gas migration. The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deteriation, and possible failures. All valves were open and the well is equipped for production. 2 Slam bar gas readings of 4% and 5% gas readings. No gauges on tubing, casing, or annulus so no pressure's recorded. The well operator was contacted and they gauged annulus psi @ 2 psi, and blew it down and left vented.

Approximately 15 gallons of produced water was spilled onto the well pad off containment. The following was observed during inspection: At the time of the inspection, I observed that SPSI appeared to have finished remediation. Approximately 60 x 60 feet of contaminated area was excavated. I observed multiple wet spots within the remediated area. No elevated conductivity was observed around the remediated/excavated and initial spill area (Photo 1-7).Logan Dominick from EQT stated in an email received on 12/05/2024 regarding spill location and updated description:On 12/3/24, we had a water truck off loading at the Comtec stands on the Gregor pad, supporting the frac. During the offloading process, the pump on the Comtec stand malfunctioned, causing the pump to back feed pressure into the truck and caused fluid to be released from the PRV on the truck. Once Environmental was able to investigate further, it was determined that the quantity was right around 1 bbl. This release is being put through Act 2. All remediation was completed the same day and consultant took confirmatory samples. Photos from Logan Dominick were included within the email, post-remediation and pre-remediation (Photo 8-10).Violations are being issued for: 78a.54, 91.34(a), CSL 301, CSL 307(a),SWMA 301, and 78a.57(a)

Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.

Comments: On 11/18/25 OGI Charles Reaggle performed a follow up inspection of the LORETTA PARKINS ET AL 3 OG well. Permit number# 129-24451. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC

Violation Code: OGA3216(D) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - ITEMS RELATED TO PRODUCTION OR STORAGE - Failure to remove production/storage facilities, supplies and equipment and restore the well site within 9 months of plugging a well.
Violation ID: 8245412
Permit API: 051-23481
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Nicholson Township
Inspection Type: Site Restoration
Inspection Date: 8/13/2025
Comments: On August 13, 2025, the Department conducted a Site Restoration inspection of Diversified's Yelenick 2 plugged well following a Well Site Restoration Submission the Department received on 7/22/2025. A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 10/24/2024, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 7/24/2025 in accordance with current regulations.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a mailbox and locked gate at the plugged well site's access road entrance. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed a Well Control and Disposal Plan as well as an Erosion and Sediment Control Plan. The beginning portion of the access road was observed to be graveled, however the remaining portion of the access road was observed to be restored and exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Upon inspection of the plugged well site, the Department observed the site to be nearing its 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth requirement with seed and mulch spread throughout its slightly less vegetated areas. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the vegetatie cover at this plugged well site to ensure it reaches its 70% uniform and adequate cover requirement. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed and no erosion and sediment control features were observed to be installed on site and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the plugged well. A pipeline riser was observed to still be present on site, the Department recommends any equipment not necessary for production of the well be removed from the site.Based on today's inspection, the Well Site Restoration Report submission is being denied due to the access road not being fully restored and the well site not yet exhibiting its 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth requirement. The Department recommends the Operator resubmit the WSRR within 60 days after restoration following the instructions for completing form 8000-PM-OOGM0075.In addition, based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to restore the well site within 9 months of plugging completion.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an inspection app IT error.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-08-20 to Minard Run Oil Co in Jenks Twp, Forest county. SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Minard Run Oil Co
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-08-20
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 859450
Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-08-20
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was from the secondary containment of a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed through a culvert under the access road and continued to spread out and flow through vegetation approximately 400 feet. Moody & Associates has been employed to coordinate the clean-up of this crude oil release. Jordan Sipos, P.G. completed the testing to establish the extent of the release and contaminated soil. Clean-up of the contaminated soil appears to be completed. Soil removal has been extended several hundred feet north of the area originally flagged as showing oil contamination from the release. Four piles of contaminated soil have been secured adjacent to the clean-up area until testing has been completed for disposal. A temporary road has been stoned to access the area and for the eventual removal of the contaminated soil. Manifest for the removal and disposal of the contaminated soil need to be submitted to the Department to lift the violations associated with this release. The removal of the contaminated soil was completed with the least disturbance possible to the surrounding vegetation and without creating a muddy unstable area. Replacement of topsoil and vegetation of this area needs to be coordinated with landowner and State Forest representatives. 15 Day initial Response Letter received July 1, 2019 for Alternate Remediation provision found in the PA DEP Oil and Gas Spill Policy. The report for the clean-up and restoration of the area needs to be submitted to the Department and approved before violations can be lifted.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/09/2024 to LEATHERWOOD LLC in Center Township, Greene county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/09/2024
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8200885
Permit API: 059-25626
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/09/2024
Comments: On 9/9/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Kentor Inc Well Pad following a produced fluid spill reported to the DEP Emergency Hotline by EQT on 9/6/2024 (CTS #383608). The spill was initially identified as staining on the ground that was discovered upon the removal of secondary containment for the Kentor 8H Well plugging operation. The spill was later updated to be greater than 5 gallons, but it was unclear the exact amount of produced fluid that was spilled onto the well pad.On site at the time of inspection was SPSI for spill remediation. SPSI indicated that they had remediated areas right of the plugged well, and a 30x60 foot area right of the plugged well was delineated by sandbags. SPSI stated that rain received on site on 9/6/2024 likely resulted in the produced fluid spill migrating out further across site. It was not clear at the time of inspection the cause of the spill nor how much produced fluid had spilled. A full spill delineation was not evident at the time of inspection. 2 rolloff boxes of impacted material were staged on site at the time of inspection, and SPSI was awaiting a third box to continue remediation.I spoke to Logan Dominick of EQT via phone call during my inspection who stated that the spill would likely be classified as an Act 2 Spill, and that the Kentor 8H Well was transferred to Leatherwood LLC to be plugged for mine-through.While on site I observed the following:-The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance and the access road appeared to be in generally good condition (Photos 1-3).-Aggregate staining as a result of produced fluid was evident immediately surrounding the left and right of the plugged well when entering the site. Aggregate was being excavated immediately around the plugged well at the time of inspection. I observed a range of conductivity readings in the stained aggregate surrounding the plugged well, varying from 2.18 mS/cm to 10.01 mS/cm. Standing fluid left of the plugged well appeared to have greater conductivity readings (Photos 4-12).-SPSI informed me while on site that they had discovered a soft spot in the aggregate on the well pad during initial remediation approximately 75-100 feet from the plugged well. Upon excavating this soft spot, produced fluid began filling up the hole. I observed conductivity readings of 10.01 mS/cm of the produced fluid standing within the hole, and the soil/aggregate read at 1859 us/cm (Photos 13-15).-Staining on the ground approximately 20 feet from the excavated hole with produced fluid within it resulted in normal conductivity measurements (Photo 16).-I observed conductivity readings of 5.65 mS/cm of standing fluid within the 30x60 ft spill delineation. Standing water located behind a black tarp at the edge of the delineated area demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 17-21).-At the time of inspection, SPSI was excavating surficial aggregate/soil that was demonstrating overall conductivity readings of 4 mS/cm (Photos 22-23).-Standing fluid within a sump/trench dug near the left-side of the Kentor Well Site demonstrated normal conductivity (Photos 24-25).Violations of 91.34(A), 78a.57(a), 78a.54, and SWMA 301 are being issued for the spill. In addition, The Department is requesting Leatherwood LLC's Kentor 8H Well plugging secondary containment plan and the maintenance records associated with the secondary containment used in the plugging process.

Comments: On May 21, 2025, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Apollo's Dewitt 1 well located in Georges Township, Fayette County in response to IR 3924375 where violations were issued for failure to stabilize the access road. IR 3928781 documents the Operator response the Department received from Apollo Resource's representative James Stiffler on 2/2/2025, which stated that the hose the Department observed on the ground is equipment that is used for production, that they will grade the access road, and that they will confirm the well tag. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed what appears to be third-party disturbance along the beginning half of the access road. Grading and brush removal is observed until the road splits off in two direction, one of which leading directly to the Dewitt Well site. This portion of the road that leads to the well site is not graded and is still exhibiting signs of destabilization. The ruts previously observed during IR 3924375 appear to be deeper and filled with stormwater. The Department is requesting the Operator report any third party disturbance to the Department. At the time of this inspection, the well site was exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. Some minor rutting was also observed within the well site from what appears to be tire tracks. The Department is again recommending the Operator conduct maintenance on the access road to stabilize it and prevent any further erosion and sedimentation issues from occurring.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag fixed to the wellhead that has incorrect Operator information posted on it, the Department is again recommending the Operator update the well tag to have accurate information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead.A meter box was and production tank was observed on site, the meter box had a well posting on it with the Operators information on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from the production tank or meter box. Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to stabilized the access road shall remain outstanding at this time.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8182509
Permit API: 081-21941
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/09/2024
Comments: Site inspection conducted to inspect 13,000 barrel Modular Aboveground Storage Structure (MASS) and site secondary containment. Meeting on site today with EQT Company Man Matt Casler. Weather conditions are sunny and 59 degrees F.According to Mr. Casler, Next Tier is on site conducting hydraulic fracturing operations for nine wells at the Mallory A Pad. The crew is zipper fracking four wells at time of inspection (1H, 3H, 5H, 17H). Pressure testing is under way for the 3H well ahead of the next pumping stage. Three wells are now complete and two wells are yet to be started. Approximately 190 stages are left for stimulation among the remaining wells. The remaining work is expected to take about three weeks. During this inspection, the Department observed secondary containment and berms which appear to be functioning as designed. All fluid transfer lines from the off load area(photo 6) to the MASS appear to be in good condition and no leaks or spills were observed. Fresh gravel is in place near areas remediated from earlier spills. Puddled fluid and damp soils on the pad were screened for elevated electrical conductivity during this inspection. Meter readings were observed to be less than 1mS/cm on pad rock surface adjacent to the main secondary containment structure and the MASS. There are no new violations noted.The Department requests EQT provide containment inspection and repair logs for dates 3/19/24-4/9/24 to juabbott@pa.gov. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21938 for the 3/1/24 produced fluid release and against permit 081-21941 for the 12/21/23 produced fluid release. The violations will remain outstanding until attainment of Act 2 remediation standards.

Comments: On 10/23/25 Casey Baldwin, O and G WQS and I were at the Coterra Energy Lauer D. Well Site in Springville Twp., Susquehanna County from 1057 to 1301 hours in response to a well control incident that occurred around 8 AM on 10/22/25. An unknown amount of natural gas and production fluid released out of the 12H well as a result of the well control incident. The weather conditions are overcast skies and chilly with light to moderate west winds, occasional gusts, and temperatures around 50 degrees Fahrenheit. The intent of the inspection is to determine if an impact occurred to the ground surface outside of the Limit of Disturbance (LOD) due to the well control incident.Shortly after arrival we met with Mike Oakley, CHMM, and Environmental Health and Safety Specialist of Coterra and the Coterra contractor Resource Environmental. The Department, Coterra, and Resource walked around the entire perimeter of the well pad and tank pad near the site LOD in a clockwise direction to determine if an impact occurred. We started just west and off the intersection of the site access road and Garrison Road near the Site ID signage. The Department utilized a Hanna Groline HI 98331 Soil Test Meter and an Oakton PCTS 5 meter to perform field conductivity screening of wet soil and small pools of fluid on the surface of the ground off the well pad. Resource utilized a Hanna HI 98192 meter. Conductivity readings do not indicate the release of production fluid has extended off the well pad. See photos for additional details.If you have any questions, do not hesitate to contact me @ 570-346-5533 or jsassi@pa.gov.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID 765666
Permit API 117-21725
Unconventional Y
County Tioga
Municipality Middlebury Twp
Inspection Type Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date 2016-08-08
Comments The Department of Environmental Protection inspected the SWEPI LP – Cruttenden 846 well pad in Middlebury Twp., Tioga Co. on 8/8/2016 @1300 hours. The weather was 80° and sunny. An adequate site ID sign was located at the entrance to the access road. An E&S inspection was last conducted by company personnel on 8/2/2016 with “no change” noted in the comments section. A small erosion channel was visible along the south side of the access road. Silt sock was visible along the access road to the tank pad. Secondary containment around the produced fluid tank contained a small amount of water with a field tested conductivity of ~700µS/cm. A hose connected the produced fluid tank to a battery of temporary tanks, located on containment, on the NE corner of the pad. Two large puddles were observed between the production equipment and the battery of temporary tanks. Puddle 1 had a field conductivity of 4.17 mS/cm. Puddle 2 had a field conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. Conductivity was tested with an Eutech Instruments Oakton Multi-Parameter PCSTestr 35. A sample was collected from puddle 1 and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for SAC 942 analysis. After receiving notification of puddles on the pad surface exhibiting elevated conductivity, SWEPI LP deployed a vacuum truck to the site and completed removal of the standing water from the pad surface the same day. SWEPI plans to proceed with removal of the temporary water tanks and containment over the next week. SWEPI stated they plan to monitor the soil conductivity readings on the pad surface and evaluate the need for additional work. SWEPI plans to notify the WQS if additional soil remediation or water collection is needed. This constitutes a violation of 25 Pa. Code §78.54 (relating to Oil and Gas Wells) against the Cruttenden 846S 24H well, API#117-21725, for failure to control and dispose of fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, production fluids and drill cuttings in a manner that prevents pollution of the water of this Commonwealth. This violation was immediately corrected. I departed the site @ 1415 hours. Please contact me with any questions. SWEPI plans to notify the WQS if additional soil remediation or water collection is needed.
